To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
outcome dependency reduces the correspondence bias, especially when it is important to predict the actor’s behavior.
the correspondence bias is reduced when perceivers’ dependency on the actor is high and the behavioral freedom is low.

the correspondence bias is reduced among dependent participants when the potential costs of a wrong dispositional inference are higher and when participants have to judge an aspect of the target’s behavior that is highly relevant to predicting their own outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the correspondence bias depends on the perceiver’s dependency on the target person, and it demonstrates the role of attention and accuracy motivation for reducing the bias.
the conditions under which outcome dependency reduces the correspondence bias.

the effects of outcome dependency on the correspondence bias and shows that outcome dependency can reduce the bias when participants are motivated to predict future behavior that affects their own outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
outcome dependency does not reduce the correspondence bias but rather increases it when it is not associated with enhanced attention and accuracy.

the correspondence bias is reduced when perceivers are dependent on the actor and when the judgment task is highly relevant to the prediction of future behavior that could affect perceivers’ own outcomes, but only when the potential costs of making an inaccurate inference are high.
the correspondence bias is reduced among outcome-dependent participants, but only when they are motivated to predict behavior that can affect their outcomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
outcome dependency reduces the correspondence bias, but only in situations in which the dispositional inference is highly relevant for the dependent participant.
the correspondence bias depends on the degree of outcome dependency and the relevance of the dispositional inferences to the outcome.

the correspondence bias is not a fixed bias, but a function of the interplay between the perceiver’s goals, motivations, and the context of the judgment. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2012 APA, all rights reserved)
The main takeaway from our work is that
outcome dependency does not necessarily increase correspondence bias but can actually reduce it under certain conditions.
correspondence bias is not necessarily an inevitable consequence of outcome dependency.
outcome dependency may reduce correspondence bias when the judgment of the actor is relevant for predicting the actor’s future behavior.
